text:
Gavin McKenna arrived in Toronto as the first overall pick with a Penn State season and a World Juniors star turn (14 points in seven games) behind him, and his first month has been a real NHL education. He has 11 points in 17 games at 18 years old, but seven of them came on the power play, and this week he was moved off the first unit. Yahoo Sports carried his reaction: "Not Too Butthurt About It." That is a healthy line from a teenager, and the Toronto Sun has written about his maturity.

The 5v5 numbers explain the demotion. Toronto has had under 39% of the chances with him on the ice, more than eight points worse than without him, and his ice time over the last ten games is down about two minutes. He is fast (97th percentile top speed among NHL skaters) and his own chances are good for his minutes. Of the four closest recent top picks, Celebrini and Bedard put up 0.9 points a game in their first full seasons; Slafkovsky and Lafreniere took years. Our projection is about 46 points. Watch the new line with Dakota Joshua.
headline: McKenna's first lesson: life on the second unit
